title: scan() doc says 'After yielding an error the scanner continues' but doesn't explain the mixed Ok+Err output for decode errors
description: uuencoding/src/lib.rs scan() doc (line 227): 'After yielding an error the scanner continues past the offending block so that subsequent valid blocks are still returned.' This is accurate for begin-base64 errors but misleading for decode-line errors: for a block with bad data lines, the scanner emits one Err per bad line AND then emits an Ok(ScannedBlock) for the same block at the end. A caller reading only the doc comment would not expect to receive both errors and a successful block from the same logical block. The error continuation behavior needs to be precisely documented.
acceptance_criteria: Expand the scan() doc comment to explain: (1) begin-base64 → one Err, scanner skips to ==== and continues; (2) malformed begin line → one Err, scanner advances one line; (3) decode error on data line → one Err per bad line, followed by one Ok(ScannedBlock) with is_truncated covering the partially-decoded data.
close_reason: Added comprehensive error-continuation documentation to scan() doc comment covering all three error cases (done as part of MIME-gcz.10)
